sections.h2: Where is Barbour County, West Virginia, and what is it like?
sections.html:
Barbour County sits on the Allegheny Plateau in north-central West Virginia, with Philippi as the county seat. It covers 342.9 square miles of mountainous country drained by the Buckhannon, Middle Fork and Tygart Valley rivers.

The Virginia legislature created the county on March 3, 1843, from parts of Lewis, Harrison and Randolph counties, and named it for the Virginia jurist Philip Pendleton Barbour. It borders Taylor and Preston counties to the north, Tucker and Randolph to the east, Upshur to the south and Harrison to the west. Laurel Mountain, the westernmost of the high Allegheny ridges, marks the eastern edge.

U.S. 119 and U.S. 250 run the length of the county, north to south, and U.S. 33 cuts across the southern tip. Philippi had 2,928 residents in 2020 and Belington, the second-largest town, had 1,804.

sections.h2: What is the history of Barbour County and Philippi?
sections.html:
Philippi was the site of what is generally considered the first land battle of the Civil War among organized troops, fought before dawn on June 3, 1861. About 3,000 federal troops under Col. Benjamin F. Kelley routed roughly 800 newly recruited Confederates. The Battle of Belington, or Laurel Mountain, followed on July 7 to 11, 1861.

Philippi's covered bridge, which carries U.S. 250 across the Tygart Valley River, was built by Lemuel Chenoweth in 1852 and is still the town's best-known landmark. The railroad reached Philippi on January 25, 1884. The last passenger train stopped there in 1956, and the line now carries only freight. The 1911 depot has been the Barbour County Historical Museum since 1979.

The county courthouse was completed in 1905. If you hold an older house in the county, a deed or survey may reference these historic roads and river bottoms, so keep the paperwork together for a buyer.

sections.h2: How does flooding affect houses in Philippi and Barbour County?
sections.html:
Philippi sits mostly on low bottomland along the Tygart Valley River, and it has flooded repeatedly. The most damaging flood came in November 1985, and the town has since adopted a floodplain management plan.

If you own a house in a river bottom, take these steps before you sell:

  • Ask your insurer or title company whether the parcel is in a mapped flood zone.
  • Collect any repair invoices from past water damage.
  • Disclose past water in the basement or crawl space to every buyer.
  • Find out whether the lender on a financed buyer will require flood insurance.

Flood questions slow down financed purchases, since lenders and insurers have to sign off. A buyer paying cash does not need a lender's approval, though a careful buyer will still look at the risk.

sections.h2: What drives the Barbour County economy?
sections.html:
Natural resources have defined the local economy: coal, gas and timber, plus family farms in the valleys. Hardwood logging boomed at the start of the twentieth century, and second- and third-growth timber is still cut each year. Oil reserves were mostly depleted early in the century.

Coal output fell from a 1948 high of 3,895,803 tons to just over 2.3 million tons in 2021, then rose to more than five million tons by 2025, making Barbour the state's ninth-leading coal county and one of the fastest-growing. That swing shows how closely household finances here can follow commodity cycles.

Alderson Broaddus University, a Baptist institution that began as Broaddus Institute in 1909 in Philippi, closed permanently in 2023. Owners near the former campus who counted on university-related demand should ask a local agent or appraiser how the closure has affected their street.

sections.h2: How is West Virginia property tax assessed, and how does Barbour County fit in?
sections.html:
West Virginia assesses all real and tangible personal property, with limited exceptions. As of July 1 each year the ownership, use and value of property are fixed for the next calendar tax year. The county assessor values your property, and the county sheriff bills and collects the tax.

The state constitution divides property into four classes:

  • Class I: intangible personal property and certain farm personal property. Nothing is currently taxed in this class.
  • Class II: owner-occupied residential property used only for residence, and farmland used for agriculture by its owner or a bona fide tenant.
  • Class III: property outside a municipality that is not in Class I or II.
  • Class IV: property inside a municipality that is not in Class I or II.

That matters at a sale. A house you live in is Class II, while a rental or vacant house falls in Class III or IV depending on where it sits, so the tax can change after the buyer takes ownership. Property tax is levied by county boards of education, county commissions, municipalities and the State.

Protests of an assessment must be filed with the county commission sitting as a board of equalization and review, which begins meeting on February 1 and must adjourn by February 28. The protest has to come before the taxes are due for that year. A disagreement over classification or taxability can go to the Tax Commissioner under West Virginia Code 11-3-24a, and the ruling is due by the end of February.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the West Virginia homestead exemption?
sections.html:
West Virginia Code 11-6B-3 exempts the first $20,000 of assessed value of a homestead from ad valorem tax. The owner must be 65 or older, or certified as permanently and totally disabled, and must use and occupy the home only as a residence.

The owner must also have been a West Virginia resident for the two consecutive calendar years before the tax year. An owner who receives a similar exemption in another state is not eligible.

If you plan to sell, the exemption matters less to you than to the buyer. A new owner under 65 will not carry it over, so the tax bill may rise. Mention that to a financed buyer's agent so there is no surprise at the first tax ticket.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Barbour County?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Barbour County follows the normal West Virginia closing steps without a buyer's mortgage. You describe the house, receive a written offer and choose whether to accept. An attorney or title company records the deed, pays off liens and settles any tax due.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses as-is. We charge no fees, commissions or closing costs, and you owe nothing if you decline. If taxes are unpaid, ask the sheriff's tax office for the balance before you set a closing date, because unpaid current-year tax can be settled out of your proceeds.

Sellers in a rural county can run into a few common problems:

  • Long distances for buyers, which can mean fewer showings on a listed house.
  • Older houses with plumbing, roof or septic questions.
  • Inherited property with several heirs in different states.

faqs.q: When are Barbour County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Tax tickets are issued on or after July 15. The first installment is due September 1 and the second March 1, with delinquency starting October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Barbour County assessment?
faqs.a: File a protest with the county commission sitting as the board of equalization and review. It begins meeting on February 1 and must adjourn by February 28, before the taxes are due.

faqs.q: Who gets the West Virginia homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Owners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, who live in the home can exempt the first $20,000 of assessed value. The application deadline is December 1.

faqs.q: Is Philippi in a flood area?
faqs.a: Much of Philippi is low bottomland along the Tygart Valley River and has flooded, most severely in November 1985. Ask your insurer or title company about your parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Barbour County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax is usually paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Get a balance from the sheriff's tax office first.

faqs.q: Does Cash Home Buyers charge fees in Barbour County?
faqs.a: No. We buy as-is with no fees, commissions or closing costs to you, and you owe nothing if you turn the offer down.
